title: Require agents to use the slicer CLI for all roadmap reads and edits
lead: Make the CLI the required interface for agents inspecting or changing slicer tracking state. This applies during reviews, planning, implementation, and validation.
findings_note: Owner request during 2026-10-02 roadmap review: the agent read tracking files directly instead of dogfooding slicer
boundary: **Not in this slice:** banning reads of ordinary source code or project documentation; changing state schemas; adding CLI features; editing generated skill text by hand.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: A roadmap review read .slicer/config.json and generated roadmap and slice files directly. That bypassed the product being reviewed and failed to exercise its supported read commands. Existing guidance prohibits manual JSON edits and generated markdown reads, but does not state one consistent rule for all tracking reads.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body: AGENTS.md; docs/agents.md; applicable project markdown guidance; src/slicer/ai.py, which generates slicer ai instructions and slicer ai skill; the checked-in slicer skill when present; focused agent-guidance tests; CHANGELOG.md.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. The published instructions and skill explicitly require the slicer CLI for both reading and changing roadmap, goals, items, slices, notes, history, and roadmap prose.
2. Guidance prohibits directly opening, searching, parsing, or editing .slicer tracking JSON, history files, and generated roadmap/slice output to obtain or change tracking state.
3. The skill covers roadmap review and planning as well as implementation, and distinguishes handing off work for review from marking reviewed work done.
4. Examples map goals to goals, inventory to list/status/stats, slice detail to show/next --ready, search to find, prose to prose show/list, and validation to check.
5. Guidance says that a missing or failing CLI capability is reported and proposed as a roadmap item, rather than bypassed with direct tracking-file access.
6. Source code, ordinary project documentation, templates, and the skill itself remain readable when needed for implementation; a task explicitly authorizing inspection or repair of tracking internals may permit that bounded exception.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Update contributor and agent guidance with one consistent CLI-first rule that applies at every stage, including roadmap reviews and planning. Extend the skill's scope to cover those tasks and include a short pointer for review handoff. Change the source shared by slicer ai instructions and slicer ai skill, then regenerate any checked-in skill through its established workflow. Replace guidance that recommends direct reads of generated roadmap files for agents with CLI commands. Preserve human-facing browsing documentation and the permission rules for commits and publication. Scope the prohibition to tracking state and generated projections, so agents can still inspect implementation code and the guidance they need to update. Tell agents to use this checkout's PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer when the editable-install warning identifies another worktree.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: Read back slicer ai instructions --json and slicer ai skill, and confirm both contain the same rule. Run the focused agent-guidance and documentation coverage tests, then the required project suite, slicer check, and git diff --check. Perform a roadmap review entirely through CLI read commands; report any failure instead of reading tracking files directly.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Leave changes reviewable. Commit and publish only when explicitly authorized by the owner.
